task: An analysis of batch vs stream processing for the clickstream pipeline: latency, cost, complexity, and a justified recommendation.

criteria.text: Latency: batch data is up to about 24 h 45 min old (a day's window plus the 45-minute job) vs seconds for streaming; notes that the dashboards refresh once a day, so the extra freshness has no consumer today.

Cost: works from the given volumes (50M events × 500 B ≈ 25 GB/day; about 600/s average, 3,000/s peak ≈ 1.5 MB/s) and compares one 45-minute daily job with always-on infrastructure sized for the peak.
Complexity: streaming needs exactly-once or idempotent processing, watermarks and late-data handling, state management and always-on operations, while batch needs only a simple rerun or retry.

A recommendation consistent with the facts (for example keep batch, or micro-batch, while dashboards are daily; move to streaming only if a real-time consumer appears), justified with the numbers above.
